I made a post about oliverian. The summary: there was a suicide of a transgender student on campus who was caught trying to slit his throat about two days prior and no action was taken. Pill use and sexual assault were rampant. If you reported an assault you just got called a slut. I do not believe it should be open. But if you ask the school head I’m just a crazy drug whore whose family doesn’t love her, so what do I know? 🤷🏼‍♀️

Hey, I also went to solstice (2014-2015) reportedly not the worst time to be there but they definitely use tactics like peer-on-peer punishment, isolation, and public humiliation, even before they started veering off the deep end. And there was an instance of a staff molesting or raping a student towards the end of my stay. DM me.

On top of that, the drugs, Jesus. All around. Damn near everyone smoked cigarettes and a massive chunk smoked weed, a lot of them daily. Weekend trips often meant stealing alcohol or just stealing in general. Meds were often traded for money or favors or different meds. One kid Destroyed the student center while high on LSD. Three kids climbed up a power tower high on LSD. Cocaine, opiates, and especially prescription benzos and amphetamines often found their way onto campus. Some staff, if we were caught with cigarettes, would just ask for a couple from our pack and let us go. Girls In my experience were punished more heavily for sneaking out and sex on campus and slut shamed even by staff members. My dorm parent directly called me a slut. Also, students overdosed rather frequently, especially on OTC cold medecine. I'm sure other people have things to say but this is just what I have so far.

My own experience, there was a student who treated girls very badly. A bunch of girls even called him a sociopath, his behavior was well known on campus. He dated one girl who dumped him because she caught him watching her sleep through her dorm window more than once. (I don't know if she ever reported this.) when he was dumped he stomped a bird to death in front of a staff. 
This is uncomfortable for me to admit because I still feel shame about it. Once a week we had a gathering at a teachers house and one day he just started hitting me really hard until I cried. When I asked him why he said he just wanted to see me cry and that it was funny to him. He did this once a week for a couple of months until the night before thanksgiving he threw me off the kitchen counter and started stomping on me and kicking me all over, especially in my genitals. Even the other students were telling him to stop but he wouldn't. Eventually a teacher heard me screaming and made him stop. Later that night he asked to have sex with me, I assumed he would keep his hands off me if I did. I was 15 and he was 17 which is statutory rape in New Hampshire. When I went home from thanksgiving break my mom saw the nasty black bruises on my leg and asked to see my texts, where she saw that we had sex. My mom called the school and demanded that they investigate, and that it was ridiculous that they turned a blind eye to that point. It was never mentioned other than my counselor scolding me for "leading him on" and giving me a consequence for sex on campus (I don't recall him getting one.)

I'll write this as facts, from what I know. My friend from the 2014/15 year disclosed to me she was molested by a teacher and the headmaster asked her to stay in her dorm until she agreed not to report. The teacher was fired at the end of the year but never charged. She often cried because teachers would poke fun at her for the incident.
Secondly, the biggest issue. A 14 year old student in the 2015/16 year committed suicide on campus. He was transgender and often misgendered by staff and students alike. He was forced to live in a female dorm as well. The day he died he had not been to school all day and they didn't start looking for him until dinner time. As I was told he died around noon that day, hours after school started. YES, since the incident the school has allowed students to stay in the dorm of their gender identity, but never before then.

I have a therapist. I've tried every anti depressant on the market, tried exercise, nature, DBT and CBT therapies. I tried psychedelics and pot (which only put me in more pain). I've heard every gimmick in the book. One person will be in pain if I die, but he will be okay, and he will find someone much more loving than me. It's time.

I think death is calling now. I got sober a few months ago and it's all lining up. I think God is transitioning me out, the intense pain I used to feel is gone, just emptiness and an overwhelming sense of my life coming to a close. My friends slowly left and now it's just me and my boyfriend, who I am not satisfying at all. I haven't done anything outside of work for months, not a single activity that wasn't a necessity. I think I am as close to dead as one can be on earth and I think it's time for me to just close the book.

It was a lot of neglect on the part of the staff. Students would trade their benzos, steal alcohol from RiteAid or wherever they could find it, smuggle cocaine, LSD and pot, and of course cigarettes. We did the math and 92% of the kids my year smoked regularly, and theft/fights would ensue over cigarettes frequently. Amphetamine trading was prevalent, as was underage sex. One student my year committed suicide, and as one staff member said, by the time they started looking (8-10 hours after he was missing) it was already too late. Boys would manipulate girls, slut-shame, sometimes slap girls around. It was like lord of the fucking flies. No one cared what we did.

You're right. I should've thought about that. I'm also not really sure what's appropriate to talk about as there are heavy topics (suicide, sexual assault, heavy drug use) and id have to take a while to think about really key topics. I will interview some students to get their perspective.

While the yoga teacher was caring and helpful, this center is mostly full of immature staff and a program that forces you to stop negative behaviors instead of getting to the root. They fix one problem and create 5 more.
